This page is the interactive version of the lesson notes (PDF). Each section
starts with a problem in a game studio. Then it explains how to analyse a
phone sheet. It ends with a **Do it** task and one set of questions. The
full explanations, examples and exercises are in the notes.

## Key terms

{{< glossary specifications chipset refresh-rate touch-sampling-rate battery-capacity sensor benchmark sustained-performance compatibility bottleneck >}}

## 8.1 Read a phone sheet like a game developer

- An advert shows the camera and the screen size first. A developer reads
  the lines that change how a game runs.
- **Chipset:** how fast the CPU and the GPU are. **RAM:** how big a game can
  be (shared with the GPU). **Display:** resolution and refresh rate.
  **Touch sampling:** how fast taps arrive. **Battery:** hours of play.
  **OS:** can it install at all. **Storage:** the free space. **Sensors:**
  tilt, turning, position.
- Lines that rarely matter: the camera (only AR and photo games), the
  weight, the colours, the charging speed.
- Phone P6: 8 cores, 2.8 GHz, mid-range GPU; 8 GB; 120 Hz, touch 240 Hz;
  5000 mAh; Android 14; 256 GB (90 GB free); accelerometer, gyroscope,
  compass, GPS; camera 64 MP.

![The sheet of phone P6.](images/phone-sheet.png){width=88%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
"200 MP camera, 6.8-inch screen" says almost nothing about how a game runs.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/sheet-filter.html" poster="sims/sheet-filter.png" title="Sheet Filter: the lines that matter for a game" height="760" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · The full sheet of your phone"}
Search the web for "*your phone model* specifications". Copy six lines:
chipset, RAM, display (with the refresh rate), battery, OS and sensors. Mark
one line that does not matter for most games.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Which lines matter?"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the colour|the weight"}
Which line tells how fast the GPU is?
:   the chipset

Which line tells if a game can be installed at all?
:   the OS version

Which line tells how fast taps reach the game?
:   the touch sampling rate

For which games does the main camera matter?
:   AR and photo games

Phone P6 has a gyroscope. Which controls does this allow?
:   aiming by turning the phone
:::
:::

## 8.2 Which phone suits which game?

- Every game loads the phone in its own way.
- **Rhythm or shooter:** touch sampling, refresh rate, steady fps.
  **AR pet game:** gyroscope, camera, strong SoC. **Big 3D world:** GPU,
  RAM, free storage. **Long sessions:** battery, little heat. **Walking map
  game:** GPS, battery, mobile data.
- Byte Bay's test phones:
  - **P5:** 8 cores, 2.2 GHz, basic GPU; 4 GB; 20 GB free; 60 Hz, touch
    120 Hz; 5000 mAh; accelerometer and GPS, **no gyroscope**.
  - **P6:** 8 cores, 2.8 GHz, mid-range GPU; 8 GB; 90 GB free; 120 Hz,
    touch 240 Hz; 5000 mAh; accelerometer, gyroscope, compass, GPS.
  - **P7:** 8 cores, 3.3 GHz, top GPU; 12 GB; 300 GB free; 120 Hz, touch
    480 Hz; **4500 mAh**; accelerometer, gyroscope, compass, GPS.
- Rhythm game: P5's taps arrive latest. AR pet game: P5 cannot run it (no
  gyroscope: a compatibility problem). 3D world that needs 8 GB: P5's RAM
  is the bottleneck.

![Different games need different lines.](images/game-needs.png){width=88%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Testing only on the best phone hides the problems most players will meet.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · The best game for your phone"}
With the six lines of your phone: for which kind of game is it best, and for
which weakest? Give one line of the sheet as the reason for each.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Phone and game"}
Use the three test phones above. Choose the right answer. You can use an
answer more than once.

::: {.match extra="all three phones"}
A rhythm game: on which phone do taps arrive latest?
:   P5

An AR pet game needs a gyroscope. Which phone cannot run it?
:   P5

A 3D world needs 8 GB of RAM. Which phone is below it?
:   P5

Which phone has the smallest battery?
:   P7

Which phone has the fastest touch sampling rate?
:   P7
:::
:::

## 8.3 Reading the small print: "up to", peak and sustained

- **"Up to 3.3 GHz":** only for a short time, while the SoC is cool.
- **"Up to 22 hours of video":** a video needs little work; a game uses
  much more power.
- A **benchmark** runs the same work on every phone and gives a score.
- A short test shows the **peak**. A test of 20 minutes shows the
  **sustained performance**: the speed after the phone is warm.
- P6: 1000 → 800 after 20 minutes (keeps 80 %). P7: 1400 → 840 (keeps 60 %).
  For a long match, compare 840 with 800.
- City Quest draws 900 mA: P7 4500 ÷ 900 = 5 hours; P5 and P6 a little more
  than 5.5 hours.

![Peak and sustained performance.](images/small-print.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Peak numbers show the first minute. Players play for 20 or 30 minutes.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Your own battery test"}
Play a game for 10 minutes. Write the battery level before and after. If it
fell by 5 %, the full battery lasts 100 ÷ 5 = 20 × 10 minutes = 200 minutes.
Estimate your play time the same way.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · The small print"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the phone is broken|22 hours"}
What does "up to 3.3 GHz" mean?
:   only for a short time, while the chip is cool

P6 scores 1000 at the start and 800 after 20 minutes. Its sustained score?
:   800

P7 scores 1400 at the start and 840 after 20 minutes. How much of its peak does it keep?
:   60 %

Why is "22 hours of video" no help for a game?
:   a game needs much more power than a video

A game draws 900 mA on P7 (4500 mAh). How long can the player play?
:   about 5 hours
:::
:::

## Game challenge: test phones for Beat Lane {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

*Byte Bay* will release *Beat Lane*, a rhythm game: the player taps notes to
the music, and a match lasts 30 minutes. It needs a steady 60 fps and fast
taps. The producer must find the phone that shows the problems, and choose
the phone for the store page. The test phones: **P5** (60 Hz, touch 120 Hz,
4 GB RAM, 5000 mAh), **P6** (120 Hz, touch 240 Hz, 8 GB, 5000 mAh, benchmark
1000 → 800) and **P7** (120 Hz, touch 480 Hz, 12 GB, 4500 mAh, benchmark
1400 → 840).

{{< sim file="sims/phone-picker.html" poster="sims/phone-picker.png" title="Phone Picker: which phone, and which line decides?" kind="game" height="720" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Beat Lane"}
P5: 60 Hz, touch 120 Hz, 4 GB. P6: 120 Hz, touch 240 Hz, 8 GB. P7: 120 Hz,
touch 480 Hz, 12 GB. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the battery|P6"}
On which phone do taps reach Beat Lane latest?
:   P5

Which line is the reason?
:   the touch sampling rate (and the refresh rate)

Which phone has the fastest touch?
:   P7

Which line does not matter for Beat Lane?
:   the main camera
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · A 30-minute match (harder)"}
P6: benchmark 1000 at the start, 800 after 20 minutes, 5000 mAh. P7: 1400 at
the start, 840 after 20 minutes, 4500 mAh. Beat Lane draws 900 mA. Choose the
right answer.

::: {.match extra="P5|40 % faster"}
Which phone is faster after 20 minutes of play?
:   P7, a little (840 against 800)

Which phone loses more of its speed when it is warm?
:   P7

How long does P7 last in Beat Lane?
:   about 5 hours

Which number should the producer compare for a 30-minute match?
:   the sustained score
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- A developer reads the chipset, RAM, display, touch, battery, OS, storage and sensors lines first.
- The camera, the weight and the colours rarely change how a game runs.
- Each game type needs other lines: touch for rhythm, gyroscope for AR, RAM and GPU for 3D worlds.
- "Up to" values and short tests show the peak; long sessions show the sustained performance.
- Test on a weak, a typical and a strong phone, not only the best one.
